column2: Again with the wheels stated before he should place the five limbs on the two hands; then the alphabet-letters enclosed by the root, with bindu,
he should place in the places of the alphabet-placing, bowing, the wise one. Then he should place the root mantra enclosed in Om as all-pervading.
By the divisions of dissolution and creation he should place the ten principles: the root-mantra syllables ending in "namah", and the others for the Self,
the principles ending in "mati" beginning with earth in order: earth, water, fire, wind, space,
ego, the great principle, Prakriti, and the supreme Person; he should place them on the head, eyes, ears, nose,
face, heart, navel, organ, knees and feet, placing the mantra's letters, interleaved with Om and ending in the heart.
This is called the placing of creation; hear the placing of preservation, O Brahmin: heart, navel, banner, knees, feet, head again,
eyes, ears, nose, face he should place in order; feet, knees, organ-place, navel, heart, face, nose,
ears, eyes, head: this is called the placing of dissolution. Creation-ending is for students; preservation-ending for householders;
the dissolution-ending is declared for the ascetic endowed with dispassion. The placing is fourfold for students, fivefold for householders,
threefold for ascetics — told in order, auspicious. Some wise ones say dissolution-ending for the dispassionate householder.
Then for obtaining the desired he should perform the Vibhuti-panjara ("cage of glory") placing, made of ten repetitions of the mantra, causing Krishna's presence:
on the base, banner, navel, heart, throat, face, bed (?), thighs, shoulder, navel, belly, heart,
breasts, sides, hips, head, face, eyes, ears, nostrils and cheeks;
so on the right arm's root, joints, tips and fingers; then on the head, in its parts beginning at the east, and in its digits;
on the arms, thighs, head, eyes, face, throat, heart and belly; the root-support, organ-place, knees and feet;
on the ear, cheek, shoulder, chest, side, and organ; on thighs, knees, shanks and feet he should place in order.
This placing named Vibhuti-panjara gives success of all aims; by this best placing he becomes Krishna's very body.
He should place the Murti-panjara placing stated before. Then he should place the ten-limb and five-limb placings in order:
in the heart, head, tuft, whole body, directions, sides, waist, back and head: the best Vaishnava should place.
Again attentive, as before he should place the five limbs with the wheels. Another heap of placings, told for the eighteen-syllable, should also be done.
Then the wise should make the all-pervading rite with the crown mantra. The best practitioner should show the flute-mudra, the bilva-mudra and others.
With the Sudarshana mantra he should do the binding of the directions. If the fingers are straight, without thumbs, the hand's branches...
this is declared the heart-mudra; so is the head-mudra. The fist with the thumb below is declared the tuft-mudra; with the hand fingers stretched is the armour-mudra.
The arrow-fist with two arms held and the thumb and forefinger: the sound; scattered all around is the weapon-mudra; where the eye is made by the forefinger and middle finger,
the left thumb at the lip, its little finger touching the right thumb and its little finger stretched,
the forefinger and ring finger slightly bent and moved: this is called the flute-mudra, kept secret, dear to Hari. The garland, Shrivatsa and Kaustubha are not mentioned, being already perfected.

Having bound the left thumb with the other hand's thumb, pressing the tip with the right fingers and firmly binding with the left hand's fingers, he should place it at his own heart-lotus and utter the Kama seed: this secret bilva-mudra, giver of all happiness, is of the lords of sages.
Whatever sin has been earned by body, mind and speech — by merely knowing this mudra, all of it is destroyed.
Meditation, chanting and worship three times stated before for the mantra: one order is declared for all, for the ten- and eighteen-syllable.
When the mantra is perfected, the mantra-knower is fit to make applications. Meditating on Krishna holding Mount Govardhana by his strong raised arm,
his mouth on the flute with the tones shown by the fingers of his other hand, he should chant the mantra, going even without an umbrella;
fear of rain, wind and lightning does not arise for him. Remembering him, the lord of the elephants, he should offer
with salt ten thousand times; drought comes, without doubt. Sporting on the bank of the Kalindi with bathing and splashing,
sprinkled by loved women with showers of water from the spray, having meditated on him, he should offer ten thousand with milk-sprinkled offerings or with water-offerings:
great rain comes even out of season, without doubt. For one afflicted by constant burning and delusion, by boils, fever and the like,
remembering him alone on the head and chanting brings peace in a moment. Or on Garuda, joined with Pradyumna and Balarama,
Achyuta praised by the fever he crushed: having meditated thus and chanted the mantra on the head of the feverish, the fevered one is freed from fever.
Having meditated and worshipped in fire, he should offer ten thousand pieces of amrita (guduchi) four fingers long, as stated, for the quieting of fever.
Meditating on Hari who removes the fearful heat pierced by arrows, touching the sufferer with both hands, he should chant for the quieting of fever.
Meditating on him giving back to Sandipani his son, he should offer ten thousand pieces of amrita as stated, to avert untimely death.
Meditating on him with Arjuna giving a son to the Brahmin whose son had died, he should chant a hundred thousand for increase of sons and grandsons.
Having offered ten thousand putrajiva fruits soaked in sweet juice, in a fire kindled with its wood, he gets long-lived sons.
At night having filled a pot with milk and worshipped it, in the morning having chanted ten thousand, he should sprinkle the woman for ten days;
thus done, even a barren woman gets long-lived sons. In the morning, silent, water in a packet of ashvattha leaf,
chanted a hundred and eight times, a woman desiring a son should drink for a month; even a barren woman gets a son with all marks.
Having conquered the witchcraft sent by the king of Kashi against his own enemy, meditating on Hari burning his city with his radiance,
the mantra-knower should offer seven days mustard seeds with oil; angered, (Krishna) surely destroys the very sender of the witchcraft.
Standing in a lovely divine hermitage thick with jujube trees, touching with lotus hands the body of Ghantakarna,
having so meditated he should offer a hundred thousand sesame soaked in the three sweet things; even one full of great sin becomes pure that moment.
Remembering Hari making Rukmin and Balarama hate each other when absorbed in dice, for creating enmity between two desired persons he should offer pellets of cow dung;
daily a thousand for seven days, he would cause enemies to hate each other. Raining arrows with blazing fire-mouths, riding Garuda,
running after the mass of enemies — meditating on Achyuta, with undistracted mind he should chant seven thousand.
The expulsion of enemies occurs in seven days. Meditating on the calf-lifter, carrying away the kapittha fruit,
chanting ten thousand, he drives out the enemy at once. Meditating on himself as Kamsa's slayer, who threw Kamsa down from the platform,
dragging Kamsa's body, lifeless, he should chant the mantra. At night, ten thousand with fuel from the tree of the enemy's birth-star,
he should offer; thus even a fierce rival goes to death. Or offering ten thousand with neem oil and oil of the rakshasa-tree,
restrained at night he soon kills enemies. At night with leaves, pepper, cotton and bone-hands...
offering with castor oil in a cemetery for the quieting of an enemy. Killing is not approved; if he does, he should offer ten thousand;
or for peace with calm mind offer as many with milk-rice. Meditating on Krishna stealing the parijata, he should chant the mantra a hundred thousand;
he has victory everywhere, never defeat. Meditating on Krishna in the chariot with the explaining-mudra hand,
showing to Partha the meaning of the Gita, a good man for the increase of dharma should chant; with pavasha flowers smeared with honey, a hundred thousand offering for gain of learning.
For protecting a kingdom, city, village, property and the body: the wearer of the universal form, bright as ten million suns rising,
Krishna of the nature of Agni and Soma, bright as molten gold, his face and feet lit by sun and fire, with divine lotus ornaments,
bearing many weapons, come to occupy the space of the universe: having meditated, he should chant a hundred thousand attentively for protection.
One who worships Hari at day's start with red forest flowers, chanting a hundred and eight times by the rule told for midday,
subdues talkative Brahmins within a thousand circles; with jasmine flowers Kshatriyas, remembering him in cowherd dress;
meditating on Krishna at play, with red hayari flowers he subdues Vaishyas, with blue lilies Shudras, remembering him,
engaged in song and dance; having offered seven days daily with white flowers and rice with ghee, and wearing the ash on forehead and head,
he would subdue a beloved woman, and she would likewise surely her husband. Betel, flower, cloth, collyrium and sandal
chanted over a thousand times with the mantra, whoever he gives it to — that man soon comes under his sway, with sons, animals and kin.
Meditating on Hari in Vrindavana with the gopis, having offered with apamarga fuel-sticks he would subdue the world.
The best Vaishnava who, having received initiation from a true teacher, worships Krishna by this rule becomes lord of the eight powers.
By merely seeing him disputants lose their brilliance; Sarasvati dwells in his mouth, and in his house the assembly-members.
Having enjoyed many kinds of pleasures, at the end he goes to Vishnu's abode.
Likewise the boy-bodied Krishna and Govinda again; hence the ten-syllable becomes a mantra with thirty-two syllables.
Of these two the sage is Narada; the metres are Trishtubh/Ushnih and Anushtubh; the deity is Nanda's son; the application is for obtaining all.
Worship should be with the five limbs by the wheels; the limbs, guardians of the directions and weapons. He should meditate on the Lord embraced by two goddesses,
holding in the right hand a jewelled cup and in the left a golden vessel. A hundred thousand chants, a tenth part offered with milk-rice.
With these two perfected mantras the mantra-knower may do as he wishes. Om, Kamala, Maya, "namo Bhagavate",
then "Nandaputraya", afterward at the end of "bala", "vapushe": this nineteen-less-one syllable mantra; Brahma is declared the sage;
the metre is Anushtubh, the deity is Krishna himself in the boy's body. This mantra is served by the wise for success of all prosperity.
Om, "Bhagavate" in the dative, "Rukminivallabhaya" and ending with "svaha": a sixteen-syllable mantra is declared.
Narada is its sage, Anushtubh its metre, Rukmini's lord the deity. With the moon-eye-Veda-limb-eye syllables he should make the five limbs, and then meditate on the Lord of the gods.

May Hari protect us — wearing pure yellow, with many ornaments, embracing with his left arm his dearest, gold-bright, the lotus-garlanded one who herself embraces him in her heart's longing, holding in his other hand a gleaming golden cane.
Having meditated thus, he should chant a hundred thousand and offer a tenth part with red lotuses,
soaked in three sweet things, and worship Hari on the seat stated before, with the limbs, Narada and others, the lords of the world and their weapons.
The mantra so perfected gives all desires to the mantra-knower. "Lila-danda" ("play-staff"): the lotus feet of the one whose arm holds the playful staff...
at the end of "danda", "dhara", "agni", "adhisha", "lohita", "meghashyama", then "Bhagavan salila-sadrik",
saying "Vishnu" with two "tha": a twenty-nine-syllable mantra. Narada is its sage, Anushtubh the metre, the deity of the mantra
is Lila-danda Hari, declared with syllables Manu-sea-intellect-yuga-fire; the five limbs with the portions arising from the mantra letters, with Vedas, in order.

May he, bewildering the gopa girls and other beautiful women with the play-staff in his left hand, resting his right hand on the shoulder of his dear friend, Kamsa's slayer, of great stride, grant us divine splendour.
A hundred thousand chants, a tenth part offered with sesame and rice soaked in three sweet things, then worship the limbs with the guardians and weapons.
He who daily with respect worships Lila-danda Hari is honoured by all the worlds, and prosperity stays firmly in his house.
Smriti, "sadya", "toya", "Keshava" with the pair of "dhara": the "Bhayagnivallabha" mantra of seven syllables, giving all success.
Its sage is Narada, the metre Ushnih, "Govallabha" the deity; he should conceive the five limbs with the wheels as before.

Hari is to be meditated on standing in the midst of the herd of tawny cows, calling them, holding a flute in the right hand, a noose and a staff in the other, dark as a rain-cloud, in yellow garments, with an ornament made of peacock feathers, the enemy of the serpent.
He should chant the mantra seven hundred thousand, then offer a tenth part with cow's milk and worship on the seat; the first enclosure is the limbs.
Golden-tawny, white-tawny, red-tawny, jaggery-tawny, brown, the best tawny,
four-tawny, yellow-tawny, the best auspicious one: having worshipped the eight groups of cows with the guardians of the world and weapons,
the mantra-knower, the mantra being thus perfected, may do desire-rites: he who daily offers a thousand and eight with milk
is freed in a fortnight along with his herd; this rule applies also to the ten-syllable. Om, heart, "Bhagavate" in the dative, "Shri Govinda" it becomes:
the twelve-syllable mantra is declared; Narada is its sage; Gayatri the metre; Shri Govinda the deity. With the moon-eye-pair-element syllables all the five limbs are conceived.
He should meditate seated at the foot of the wish-tree on a divine lion-throne shining with gems, dark as a cloud, in tawny silk, very beautiful, with a conch and a staff in his two hands,
bearing a thousand cows, the lord of the immortals, bathed by the flowing stream from the palace-spout of Indra's single pot held in a mature hand, with eyes like fresh lotus petals.
He should chant the mantra twelve hundred thousand; offer a tenth with milk and worship, as before, whether in the cow-pen or in images.
On the Vaishnava seat stated before, conceiving the form from the root, invoking and worshipping Krishna after worship of the teacher,
having worshipped Rukmini and Satyabhama at the sides, Indra in front, Surabhi behind, he should worship the limbs on the filaments.
The eight queens beginning with Kali are on the Vasu-petals; at the seat's corners binding ... again the little bell,
garlands at the back, the flute, in front Shrivatsa and Kaustubha; in front the forest-garland and the rest stand in the eight directions;
the Panchajanya, mace, discus, Vasudeva and Devaki, Nanda the cowherd and Yashoda, with cows, cowherds and gopis;
Indra and the others stand outside, then Vajra and the others; Kumuda, Kumudaksha, Pundarika, Vamana,
Shankukarna, Sarvanetra, Sumukha, Supratishthita; Vishvaksena is to be worshipped, then the Self is to be worshipped.
The man who worships Govinda once or three times a day lives long, free of fear, and becomes lord of wealth and grain.
Smriti, "sadya", with the discus, with the right ear, "dhara", "nathaya", ending in the heart: this great mantra has eight syllables.
Its sage is Brahma, metre Gayatri, Krishna its deity; with the pair of letters and all the five limbs are conceived.
Bow to the cowherd child, five years old, very restless, running in the courtyard, with very mobile eyes, adorned with bells, bracelets, necklace and anklets.
Having thus meditated, he should chant eight hundred thousand and offer a tenth part with Brahma-tree fuel or milk-rice.
On the Vaishnava seat stated before, conceiving the form from the root, the mantra-knower, steady of mind, should invoke and worship Krishna there.
He should worship the limbs on the filaments in the four directions and corners; in the directions Vasudeva and Balarama, Pradyumna and Aniruddha;
in the corners Rukmini and Satyabhama, Lakshmana and Rikshaja (Jambavati); outside, the lords of the worlds with weapons. Thus the mantra is perfected.
Om, Shri, Bhuvaneshani, Kama in the dative: he should say "Shri Krishnaya", then "Shri Govindaya", then "gopijanapada",
then "vallabhaya" and three "padma": the mantra of the syllables of the principle. The sage and the rest are as told before; he should remember the accomplished Gopala.
Seated in the Madhavi bower, protected by Garuda, absorbed in divine play — remembering Rama and Krishna, he should chant.
The best Vaishnavas should worship as before. The one-syllable mantra: the discus-bearer with the sage-tone, ending with visarga.
Krishna: two-syllable; beginning with Kama, three-syllable; the same in the dative is two-syllabled: "Krishnaya namah".
Five-syllable: "Krishnaya", Kama and "ruddha" higher; "Gopalaya" ending in "agnijaya": six-syllable is declared.
Kama, "Krishna" in the dative, ending in "vahnijaya": another; "Krishna-Govindaya" in the dative: seven-syllable, giving all success.
Shri, Shakti, Kama, "Krishnaya", Kama: another seven-syllable; "Krishna-Govindaya" in the dative, ending in the heart: another, nine-syllable.
Krishnaya Govindaya in the dative, then Kama, the enclosure; Kama, Sharngi, with the earth, ... Manu, moon, and Manmatha:
Shyamalangaya hridayam: ten-syllable giving all success; "Balavapushe Krishnaya agnijaya": another;
Balavapushe with two "tha", Kama, he should say "Krishnaya". Then meditating in his heart on the one who charms the minds of the gopis:

I bow to the youth of Nanda, moon-faced, dark as a cloud, who plays on the Kalindi sands, served by the fragrant wind among the bent, blossoming creepers in the lanes of glorious Vrindavana, whose sole life is Radha.
Their worship is to be known by the path told before, O lord of sages. At the end of "Devaki-suta" he should utter "Govinda",
saying "Vasudeva", addressing the Lord of the world: "Give me a son," then "Krishna, I..."
... have come for refuge — a mantra of thirty-two syllables. Narada is its sage; metres Gayatri and Anushtubh; the deity is Krishna the giver of sons; the limbs are made with the feet and all.
Victorious, standing in the chariot, having brought the sons from the middle of the ocean, he gave them to the Brahmin — Vasudeva's son is to be remembered thus.
A hundred thousand chants, ten thousand offering with sesame soaked in sweet juice, worship on the seat stated before with the limbs, lords of the world and weapons.
When the mantra is perfected, the mantra-knower gets a son even from a barren woman. Om, Maya, then "sa" with moon and "su"...
So 'ham ending with "agnipriya": this is a supreme eight-syllable mantra. The sage of this five-Brahman mantra, best of sages,
is Brahma; the supreme Gayatri is the metre; the deity is declared "the Supreme Light, the Supreme Brahman".
Om is the seed; "svaha" is the power. "Svaha" is the heart; "So 'ham" the head;
Hamsa the tuft; "hrillekha" the armour; Om the eye; "Hari Hara" the weapon.
He is Brahma, he is Shiva, O Brahmin, he is Hari, he is the king of gods; he is of all forms, called all; he is the imperishable, supreme, self-luminous.
Having so meditated, he should chant eight hundred thousand, offer a tenth; the worship of this is held on the Om-seat with limbs and enclosures.
When the mantra is perfected, knowledge arises for the best of practitioners, O Narada — the changeless knowledge told in sayings like "That thou art".
Kama, in the dative, Hrishikesha, ending in the heart: an elephant-syllable (eight) mantra. Its sage is Brahma, metre Gayatri;
the deity is Hrishikesha; the application is for obtaining all. Kama is the seed; the power is "aya".
Having made the six limbs by the seed alone, he should perform the meditation. Everything else is declared as for the Purushottama mantra.
A hundred thousand chants, ten thousand offering with ghee alone is declared; satisfaction with the Sammohini flowers is declared for gaining all desires.
